report.title: Week 12 Scouting Report: CHI at DET (Bears at Lions)
report.summary: Chicago is balanced on early downs but shifts to the pass in long-yardage spots, and its right-side run and explosive passing are the main threats. Detroit's pass defense and red-zone defense are the soft spots to address. Chicago's third-down defense is elite, so Detroit's manageable downs are the key to the game. Special teams are roughly even, with Chicago's punting the edge to watch.

sections.heading: Opponent offense
sections.body: Chicago throws on 51.1% [oc1] of early-down plays over 521 [oc2] plays, but tilts to the pass when behind the sticks, at 68.5% [oc5] on long second downs and 84.6% [oc7] on medium-distance third downs. Its passing game is the stronger unit at 0.07 [oc14] EPA per pass play, while the run game sits at -0.03 [oc15] EPA per run play. Chicago produces explosive passes on 9.7% [oc19] of pass plays, and Detroit allows explosive passes on 8.9% [oc20] of pass plays, so shot plays are real. Designed runs go right on 55.2% [oc23] of attempts, versus 35.7% [oc25] left, and Detroit allows explosive runs on 9.8% [oc29] of carries, so the right-side run is the main threat. In the red zone Chicago scores touchdowns on 57.5% [oc31] of trips over 40 [oc32] drives, while Detroit gives up touchdowns on 67.6% [oc35] of red-zone trips.

sections.heading: Opponent defense
sections.body: Chicago blitzes on 34.6% [dc1] of dropbacks over 350 [dc2] plays, averaging 4.5 [dc3] rushers per dropback, and Detroit's offense has allowed a sack or QB hit on 16.8% [dc5] of dropbacks over 363 [dc6] plays, so the blitz is a live threat to the pocket. Chicago allows pass EPA of -0.05 [dc8] per play. Against the run it keeps 6.8 [dc10] defenders in the box, so attack the lighter boxes with the run and use play action off the same looks. Chicago is the league's best third-down defense, allowing conversions on 26.9% [dc14] of attempts and ranking 1st [dc16], which makes Detroit's manageable third-down drives the main opportunity. In the red zone Chicago allows touchdowns on 55.6% [dc17] of drives, so Detroit's red-zone package should be built to finish drives rather than wait for Chicago to break.

sections.heading: Special teams
sections.body: Chicago has used a single kicker all season, C.Santos, who has made 17 [kc1] of 21 [kc2] field goals, but only 60.0% [kc4] from 50-plus on 5 [kc5] attempts, so treat a long try as close to a coin flip. Chicago's punting is its edge to watch, with a net average of 42.8 [kc8] yards on 29 [kc9] punts. Chicago's punt coverage allows 5.8 [kc11] yards per return on 16 [kc12] returns, while Detroit averages 5.3 [kc13] yards on 28 [kc14] punt returns, so take the return. Special-teams EPA is 0.11 [kc19] per play over 257 [kc20] plays for Chicago and 0.1 [kc21] over 267 [kc22] for Detroit, so the units are roughly even overall.

sections.heading: Injuries and availability
sections.body: Chicago's CB Kyler Gordon is Out [ic2] with a shoulder injury after playing 56.5% [ic3] of snaps over 4 [ic4] games, so expect a replacement corner against Detroit's outside targets. WR Zavion Thomas is Questionable [ic5] with an ankle injury, but his 4.14% [ic6] target share over 10 [ic7] games keeps him minor. Detroit's C Cade Mays is Out [ic9] with an ankle injury after a 65.5% [ic10] snap share over 2 [ic11] games, so expect a backup at center. CB D.J. Reed is Questionable [ic12] with a hip injury at a 94.0% [ic13] snap share over 7 [ic14] games, the most significant Detroit listing. DE Tyler Lacy is Questionable [ic15] and has played 34.5% [ic16] of snaps over 10 [ic17] games.

sections.heading: Key matchups
sections.body: Start with Chicago's right-side run against Detroit's edges. Chicago runs right on 55.2% [mc1] of designed carries over 297 [mc2] designed runs, and Detroit allows explosive runs on 9.8% [mc3] of carries over 204 [mc4] plays, so keep gap integrity and rotate the ends with Lacy questionable and having played 34.5% [mc5] of snaps. Chicago brings blitz packages on 34.6% [mc6] of dropbacks over 350 [mc7] plays, so plan max protection on the interior, slide toward the backup center, and use quick throws and screens. Chicago produces explosive passes on 9.7% [mc11] of pass plays, and Detroit allows explosives on 8.9% [mc12] of pass plays over 429 [mc13] plays. With CB Kyler Gordon out after 56.5% [mc14] of snaps, test the replacement early on the boundary, while Detroit's safeties hold the top of coverage on the medium-distance and long downs when Chicago throws most.
